recipes.name: Slow Cooker Coconut Curry Chicken
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breasts, cut into cubes
1 tablespoon flaked coconut, or to taste

steps.text: Place chicken, potatoes, onion, garlic, coconut milk, chicken broth, curry powder, salt, and black pepper in a slow cooker.

Cook on Low for 4 hours. Add red bell pepper and continue to cook for 45 minutes. Stir in cornstarch and cook until thickened, about 15 minutes more. Sprinkle with raisins and coconut flakes to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Coconut Curry Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Morsels of chicken breast are slow-cooked in a creamy coconut curry with potatoes and red bell pepper. Raisins and flaked coconut add texture and sweetness to this rich dish.

review.reviewBody: I made this today exactly as it said in the recipe, we loved it. Thanks mikeyv, will defiantly make this again.

I could only give this three stars because as written, it is pretty bland, soupy and tasteless. However, the hubby and I both love curry so I experimented and came up with what I believe is a 5-star dish. I used two cans of 13.5oz coconut milk, about 1/2 cup of chicken broth, about 1 cup matchstick carrots, diced yellow potatoes, 3 yellow onions diced, about 1 tblsp freshly ground black pepper, 1/4 cup plus 2 tblsp curry, 1 tblsp of chopped garlic and sea salt to taste. I did not dice the chicken breasts since the slow cooker makes the chicken so tender. The last hour I added the red bell pepper, about a 1 and half cups of sweetened flake coconut and the cornstarch which probably wasn't needed but did thicken it a bit more. I then served it over white rice made with milk, water and butter. These changes made this an awesome dish though probably not very low calorie. However, the flavor was perfect and reminded me of a good vegetarian Vietnamese dish (basically veggies in a coconut broth). I know I could have made this without the crock pot but am always looking for slow cook recipes to help with busy schedules. Cook on Sunday, eat leftovers most of the week. :)

Easy and solid recipe! I agree with what others said about it being a starting point for more seasonings (I felt it could use more salt and needed some spice). A few tips: 1) Remove some of the liquid and whisk the cornstarch into that to make a slurry, then stir that slurry back into the pot gently (this will prevent shredding to the chicken or potatoes too much while trying to blend in the cornstarch). 2) Mine needed more than 4 hours + the additional time to soften the potatoes. 3) Don’t skip the coconut! It really gives this something extra.

This was a great recipe - I made it with shrimp as I don't eat chicken and I used vegetable broth instead of chicken broth. I cooked for 4 + hours as opposed to 5+ hours. I added cauliflower 2 hours into cooking and added the red pepper and shrimp 3 hours into cooking. 15 minutes before serving, I added a tablespoon of mustard seed (give a neat texture), cliantro and the coconut milk. I added the cornstarch too to add thickness. I also added 3/4 tablespoon of cumin and a teaspoon of cardamom powder as well as garlic powder in addition to the fresh garlic. Very yummy!

Pros: I was amazed that this recipe actually has a 1/4 c of curry powder in it. I thought it was a mistake but added 1/4 c anyway. 1/4 c is about the amount in the average size spice bottle. This recipe is easy to use as a base. I rarely follow a recipe without making my own changes. My changes were incorporated into the recipe easily and included adding carrots, eggplant and chick peas. I also added a cinnamon stick and 1/4 tsp. of nutmeg. I made Basmati rice to go with it and used 1/2 water and 1/2 of the curry broth to cook it in. 

Cons: The recipe instructions are vague. Specifically what type and size are the potatoes? I used red potatoes and they worked fine. I did a web search and found that 2 potatoes equal about 2 cups of potatoes. Since my potatoes were small I added 2 cups of potatoes which was about 4 of the type of potatoes I used. The recipe also doesn’t indicate the type or the actual amount of onion needed. I added 2 small yellow onions because that is what I had on hand. 

I was pleased with my version of this recipe but will be looking for other chicken recipes to try in the future.

This was an awesome dish and I got lots of compliments on it! 

Using what I had, I used chicken leg & thigh quarters. I omitted the raisins and the shredded coconut. I did add some turmeric.

I am rather proud of myself and will be making this dish again!

I took the advice of others and used 2 extra Tbls of Curry Powder, I added a pinch of dried Curry leaves, added sweet potatoes, and used boneless/skinless thighs. Like others I added the potatoes in the last 1-2 hours. I cooked it 8 hours on low. Next time I'll use lite coconut milk to save calories. Needs more salt, but yummy on a cold night!

Great recipe for Chicken Curry lovers! I added one can of pineapple chunks and a trio of colored peppers, red, orange, yellow to kick up the visual appeal. I also had a can of thick coconut cream (Trader Joes)on hand so I threw in two large spoonfuls of that for extra richness but the recipe is great as is. I used skin on browned chicken thighs as that is what I had on hand and the meat just fell off the bone and was very tender. If you like a colorful dish use your food processor and mince some carrot up fine then add the last twenty minutes of cooking time. This is good served over jasmine rice.

I read all the reviews before beginning, so I also added julienned carrots when I added the chopped red pepper. I also veganized it by using Butler's Soy Curls. I used a tiny bit more water as I did not know if the soy curls would soak up more liquid (I had re-hydrated them first). I did NOT add in the corn starch as I wanted the rice to soak up all the goodness. I did add 2T of brown sugar, which was unnecessary if you used the raisins. Would make this again with tofu it is delicious!

This recipe is a good base for an easy yellow curry. Now, the tweaks....We definitely always end up needing to add salt to our individual servings to bring out and meld the flavors. We also prefer more veg so add more bell pepper and I personally love sweetness for balance so I tend to add a hearty amount of raisins and coconut flake. My husband likes heat so he adds red pepper flake to his serving. Lastly, we use boneless skinless chicken thighs for a more tender slow cooker dish. All of this to say, the recipe as is probably won’t blow your mind, BUT, it’s a great jumping off point and highly adaptable to suit individual tastes.

I really enjoyed this recipe. I followed some of the suggestions in the reviews. I used 3 chicken quarters, 1/4 Curry Powder + 2T. I didn't want to open a box of broth and had a can of chicken broth and used it all so not to waste any. I set it on low 8 hrs in u crock and when I got back to it, it was falling off the bone delish!!! Will surely do again.

Easy to throw together and let its do its thing. Not sure why others said it was watered down. There’s no water in this recipe and you make a slurry with cornstarch and add last 15 minutes and mine has come out tasty and smooth every time.

Good. I used chicken thighs instead of breast and carrots in place of potatoes. Next time I would use half the chicken broth and flour as a thickener instead of cornstarch. I also added a tin of diced tomatoes.

Place a bunch of spice in water and this is what this recipe tastes like. I am new to making curry but I am not new to tasting authentic Asian cuisine. This is not authentic. Curry should have a richer taste and not be completely watered down as this is.

It was delicious. I added a bit more salt at the end, even though I am a person that always holds back on salt, but it needed a touch more. I also added a drizzle of honey, which gave it a nice flavour. Do remember to add the raisins and coconut on top, as that makes it perfect.
Like the reviews below, I thought it was a bit bland, despite the addition of Cayenne. Mine ended up a bit soupy as well.
I only gave it one star because it is required. I haven’t made it yet, have a question regarding the curry. What type of curry is everyone using?

Made this yesterday it was delicious everyone loved it! I did add more curry than the recipe called for just because I love curry! Also used both chicken breast and thighs, it definitely enhanced the flavor. Will make it again!
My first attempt at making Curry and this recipe was so easy and delicious!! A keeper for sure.
Delicious!! This has become a family favourite. My kids and hubby absolutely love this recipe. I have made it in a pot on the stove top and it’s fantastic!!
